title: The experiment that re-randomized users
blurb: Editable splits re-bucketed users mid-flight and reports peeked.
prompt: A rollout looked great because an operator shifted traffic mid-experiment, and the final report ignored a metric whose traffic had gone 70/30 instead of 50/50. The model-generated draft recomputes buckets against a mutable salt and never checks sample ratio mismatch. Review it, fix it, and prove assignment is frozen and reports are honest.
aiNote: The draft derives buckets from a hash over a salt that changes when splits are edited, so users move between variants mid-experiment and treatment effects are contaminated, and the report happily names a winner on a peek or on a mismatched split.
testIdea: Edit the split mid-experiment and assert the request is rejected; evaluate one unit before and after a salt change and assert the variant is unchanged; feed 70/30 traffic and assert the winner call is blocked with an SRM caveat.
followUps: Which unit is right for which experiment?
How do sequential tests change the peek problem?
What guardrail metrics belong in every experiment?
